findings.quote: The stated goal is positive operating cash flow by the end of the first quarter of 2027
findings.issue: The shareholder letter carries two different near-term cash-flow targets and the report silently merges them. The dedicated section 'Drive Toward Positive Cash Flow from Operations' says: 'Our next financial goal is to achieve positive cash flow, as adjusted and related to our normal operations. We are still targeting to achieve this by the end of 2026.' The 'end of the first quarter of 2027' date belongs to a different goal in the letter's opening — reaching the (higher) 'breakeven point'. The report attaches the Q1-2027 date to the 'positive operating cash flow' goal, which the letter dates to end of 2026, and never notes the disagreement. Same conflated claim recurs in analystCommentary, sections.executiveSummary.catalysts[3] and sections.finalRecommendation.body[1].
findings.fix: State the operating-cash-flow target as the letter states it (positive cash flow from normal operations, as adjusted, targeted by the end of 2026), and, if the Q1-2027 date is kept, distinguish it as the separate breakeven-point target and note the source gives two dates — per rubric item 8, say which you used.
findings.note: Fixed. cashflowCommentary now reads 'The letter sets two separate milestones, and I use both as stated: positive cash flow from normal operations, as adjusted, targeted by the end of 2026, and the higher breakeven point, which the CEO believes the company can reach by the end of the first quarter of 2027.' The 2026 target now appears in analystCommentary and catalysts[3], and finalRecommendation.body[1] lists both milestones distinctly.

findings.quote: Weighting the three cases at 30% Bull, 40% Base, and 30% Bear yields a probability-weighted fair value of about $28.60, roughly 26% above the current $22.69, with a reward-to-risk ratio below one because the Bear downside of about 43% is larger than the expected upside.
findings.issue: The scenario probabilities and the probability-weighted fair value are stated three times: in the structured scenarios array, again here in scenarioCommentary, and a third time in sections.finalRecommendation.body[0]. The reward/risk framing ('below one because the ~43% Bear downside exceeds the expected upside') is likewise repeated near-verbatim in finalRecommendation.body[1]. Rubric item 6 asks that each probability be stated and argued once, not restated in three places.
findings.fix: Argue the weighting and the $28.60 / ~26% expected value once (scenarioCommentary is the natural home) and have finalRecommendation refer back to it in words rather than re-listing the three probabilities, implied prices and the weighted value again.
findings.note: Fixed. finalRecommendation.body[0] no longer re-lists the three probabilities/implied prices/weighted value; it refers back in words ('their probability-weighted fair value sits well above today's price'). body[1] now says 'The reward-to-risk profile is deliberately skewed toward a larger drawdown than upside, as set out in the scenario discussion' rather than restating the ~43% figure. The weighting is argued once in scenarioCommentary.

findings.quote: It is deploying that capital into inventory, with raw materials and prepaid inventory rising from $25.8 million to $42.4 million in the quarter, into capital equipment, about $3.3 million of Q2 capex
findings.issue: Several exact figures are restated in more than one section rather than introduced once and referred back in words (rubric item 7). The inventory build ($25.8M to $42.4M) appears in both balanceCommentary and here. The $3.3M Q2 capex appears in both cashflowCommentary and here. The enterprise-revenue figure $14,220,865 vs $192,090 is quoted verbatim in four sections: executiveSummary.thesis, financials.incomeCommentary, businessMoat.segments[0], and growth.points[1].
findings.fix: Introduce each of these figures once (inventory build in balanceCommentary, capex in cashflowCommentary, the enterprise-revenue pair in incomeCommentary or growth) and refer back to them in words elsewhere (e.g., 'the inventory build noted above', 'enterprise sales, as shown in the income discussion').
findings.note: Fixed. capitalAllocation now refers to 'the inventory build noted in the balance-sheet discussion' and 'the capital equipment behind its motor line covered in the cash-flow discussion' with no repeated figures. The Q2 enterprise pair $14,220,865 vs $192,090 now appears only in incomeCommentary; thesis quotes the total-revenue pair and businessMoat.segments[0] refers back in words; growth.points[1] uses the distinct six-month enterprise pair ($21,510,234 vs $312,246).

findings.quote: {+ cash was approximately $229.6 million at June 30, 2026, up from $103.3 million +}
findings.issue: House style limits {+ +} / {- -} spans to the signed change or the explicit positive/negative, not the surrounding clause (rubric item 9). This span wraps the full cash-level statement when only 'up from $103.3 million' is the positive movement. The same over-wide wrapping appears in the sibling spans '{+ Q2 2026 revenue reached $16,722,467, up 687% from $2,123,970 a year earlier +}' and '{- our Bear case of $13.00 sits about 43% below the current price -}', the last of which brackets essentially a whole clause.
findings.fix: Tighten the spans to the signed element only (e.g., '{+ up from $103.3 million +}', '{+ up 687% +}', '{- about 43% below the current price -}') and leave the surrounding levels unmarked.
findings.note: Still open. The two positive spans are unchanged and still wrap the full level statements. The bear span was reworded to '{- our Bear case of $13.00 sits well below the current price -}' but still brackets essentially the whole clause rather than the negative element alone.

findings.quote: Governance rests on the DEF 14A filed 2025-10-20.
findings.issue: Rubric item 9 requires dates in prose form, not ISO. Every other date in the report is written in prose form (e.g., 'October 6, 2025', 'May 7, 2026'); this lone '2025-10-20' is ISO format.
findings.fix: Write the date in prose form, e.g., 'the DEF 14A filed October 20, 2025.'
findings.note: Still open. The governance section still reads 'the DEF 14A filed 2025-10-20' in ISO format; unchanged from round 1.

findings.quote: The proxy identifies the other named executive officers as Brian Hoff, Andrew Camden and Jeffrey Thompson; Thompson previously served as CEO and remains a director.
findings.issue: The captured proxy excerpt lists these names only under a combined beneficial-ownership table headed 'Named Executive Officers and Directors' and never disaggregates which of the seven are named executive officers versus directors. The excerpt presents Thompson as a director (not independent because he was CEO within the last three years), so labelling him a current 'named executive officer' is an inference the captured text does not make (rubric item 2/4). Hoff and Camden are supportable as executives (the MD&A grants options to 'three other executive officers'), but the specific NEO enumeration attributed to the proxy is not on the captured surface.
findings.fix: Either attribute only what the excerpt supports (e.g., 'the ownership table lists directors and officers including Brian Hoff, Andrew Camden and Jeffrey Thompson'), or drop the 'named executive officers' characterisation for Thompson, whom the proxy presents as a director/former CEO.
findings.note: Still open. The leadership sentence is unchanged from round 1; the proxy still does not disaggregate NEOs from directors and presents Thompson as a director/former CEO.
